title: Parameterizing Dark Energy at the density level: A two-parameter alternative to CPL
summary: This abstract introduces a new, two-parameter model for dark energy evolution that avoids some degeneracies found in the CPL model, and demonstrates that by combining BAO, CMB, and SN Ia data, the parameters are well-constrained and reveal a preference for evolving dark energy that remains below 3σ, consistent with previous findings.

title: Nonlinear Information from DESI Luminous Red Galaxies: An Emulator-Based Analysis of Pre- and Post-Reconstruction Power Spectra
summary: This study jointly analyzes pre- and post-reconstruction power spectra from DESI DR1 LRGs with an emulator-based framework, improving cosmological constraints, particularly in $w$CDM, by incorporating nonlinear information and Type Ia supernovae.

title: Cosmic Shear in Effective Field Theory at Two-Loop Order: Revisiting $S_8$ in Dark Energy Survey Data
summary: This paper presents a novel approach using two-loop effective field theory (EFT) to analyze cosmic shear data from DES-Y3, yielding competitive constraints on the $S_8$ parameter and suggesting new avenues for testing physics with future surveys.

title: Estimation and mitigation of foregrounds in projected kSZ velocity reconstruction
summary: This study investigates foreground contamination in kSZ-reconstructed velocity-galaxy cross-correlations, a key probe for primordial non-Gaussianity, and introduces a novel parity-odd estimator that effectively cancels foreground biases and significantly improves signal detection.

title: Can a single supernova remnant account for the gamma-ray emission of G106.3+2.7?
summary: This abstract investigates the TeV emission from SNR G106.3+2.7, exploring a supernova remnant in a clumpy environment as a potential PeVatron, but ultimately suggests a pulsar association is more likely for the broadband gamma-ray emission.

title: An Intertwined Short and Long GRB with 4-minute Separation
summary: This abstract discusses a peculiar gamma-ray burst (GRB 160425A) that exhibits characteristics of both short-duration (merger-origin) and long-duration (collapsar-origin) GRBs, challenging current progenitor models.

title: Removing the Cosmological Bound on the Axion Scale via Confinement During Inflation
summary: This paper explores a novel scenario for axion cosmology within an SU(5) grand unified theory, proposing that strong QCD during inflation can relax the axion's energy density and allow it to be a viable dark matter candidate regardless of its decay constant.

title: Investigating the $H_0$ Tension and Expansion-History Mismatch with Diverse Dark Energy Parametrization Frameworks
summary: This study investigates the $H_0$ tension by comparing $\Lambda$CDM with phenomenological dark energy models using Pantheon+ and DESI data, finding that a pressure density parametrization partially alleviates the tension by suggesting deviations primarily at low redshifts.

title: Cosmological peculiar velocities in general relativity?
summary: This abstract critiques a recent manuscript arguing for a quasi-Newtonian approach to peculiar velocities, highlighting its historical limitations and self-contradiction by pointing to earlier work by one of its authors, and advocating for the validity of relativistic treatments.

title: Single vs. Binary Origin: The Diversity of Stripped-Envelope Supernova Remnants
summary: This abstract discusses simulations of core-collapse supernova remnants from single and binary progenitors, finding differences in their evolution and spectral characteristics, and introducing a new timescale for scaling their phases.

title: Study of neutrinophilic low-mass dark matter mediated by pseudoscalar
summary: This paper explores a neutrinophilic dark matter model where traditional indirect detection is insufficient, necessitating constraints from Lyman-α forest, astrophysical neutrinos, direct detection, and invisible Higgs decays.

title: Bayesian Model Comparison of $R_h=ct$ versus $Λ$CDM using HII galaxy Hubble diagram
summary: This study uses Bayesian model comparison with HII galaxy data to show that the $R_\mathrm{h}=ct$ cosmological model is equally favored as $\Lambda$CDM/$w$CDM with uniform priors, but strongly favored over flat $\Lambda$CDM and marginally favored over flat $w$CDM when Planck priors are used.

title: Exploring the interplay of late-time dynamical dark energy and new physics before recombination
summary: This abstract focuses on novel analysis methods for SN Ia samples (DES, Pantheon+) to investigate dark energy dynamics, rather than their direct correlation with host galaxy properties.

title: Tracing the Evolution of $Ω_m(z)$ over the Last 10 Billion Years with Non-parametric Methods
summary: This abstract focuses on using Type Ia supernovae primarily as standardizable candles for cosmological parameter estimation, rather than exploring their intrinsic properties or correlations with host galaxy characteristics.
